title: Date searches did not remove the low 2020-2025 PDO mean mismatch in a model fitted to 1951-2019
abstract: We tested whether a search over dates removes a known low PDO mean mismatch. The observed 2020-2025 mean was -1.99514. We fitted monthly memory, calendar and lagged ENSO terms to 1951-2019. In 19,999 simulated 75-year histories with actual ENSO fixed and 12-month residual blocks, two had any 72-month mean this low across 829 monthly starts. None had a fixed end-period mean this low. The scan fraction was 0.00015, with a 95% simulation interval of 0.0000121 to 0.0003612. Date selection alone did not remove the mismatch under this reference. Fits through 2025 gave scan fractions from 0.00960 to 0.26990 across 3- to 72-month blocks. This large sensitivity limits an exceptional-event claim. The test adjusts only the start date at a fixed width and statistic. It omits parameter and source uncertainty and assumes stable residual blocks. The result does not establish a new climate regime or physical cause. Original code, full simulated mean statistics, source hashes, an arithmetic audit and a figure are included. External source tables remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Fixed-date and full-record search fractions change with fit period and residual block length. Error bars cover simulation sampling only. Zero counts are plotted at the plus-one floor.
